codeReview.summary: skel-detail implementation fully satisfies VAL-SKEL-005. The commit adds focused-lane state (0=Main, 1=Detail, 2=Evidence) with Tab/Shift+Tab cycling, integrates the M2 DetailPane component into renderReady via renderDetailPaneRows(), and adds 12 unit tests covering all required behaviors. All TUI package tests pass under -race; go vet is clean.

issues.description: TestDetailLane_ScrollWhenFocusedAndOverflow only verifies that DetailPane renders without panic and produces non-empty content. It does not verify that scrolling within the Detail pane actually works (e.g., that scroll offset is maintained correctly when focus changes). This is acceptable for a skeleton test but leaves scroll behavior underexercised.

CycleFocusForward briefly releases c.mu between FocusedLane() and SetFocusedLane(). The FocusedLane() call locks/unlocks the mutex, then SetFocusedLane() locks again. This creates a narrow window between unlock and lock where another goroutine could observe inconsistent state. In practice this is benign since (a) KeyMap callbacks run on the main TUI event loop (single-threaded) and (b) the final state written is deterministic. No data race is detectable, but the pattern could be tightened by reading focusedLane into a local variable under one lock.

summary: Pass. skel-detail implements VAL-SKEL-005 correctly: focusedLane state with Tab/Shift+Tab cycling, DetailPane integration via renderDetailPaneRows() mapping agent status to StatusVariant, all three required sections (Runtime/Hierarchy/Recent Activity), selection surviving Tab round-trips, empty states, focus indicator, status badge, workspace info, and parent display. 12 new unit tests cover the behaviors. No regressions; all TUI tests pass under -race. Two non-blocking observations: scroll test is shallow, and CycleFocusForward has a minor lock-release gap (benign in practice).
